parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous answer.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon. minLon > maxLon means the box crosses +/-180.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: root/leaf path; a prefix filter, so a parent finds its descendants.

parameters.name: f.<slug>
parameters.description: Facet filter. Repeat for OR within a slug; different slugs AND together.

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description: on | off | comma-separated slugs. Default is the category's plan.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Language of the query: selects the analyzer AND narrows the corpus. Omit it and only the analyzer is chosen (from Accept-Language) — a header must not hide a catalogue.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Opaque owner key — the seller's own listings.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text. Dictionary-normalized here; morphology belongs to the engine.

parameters.name: r.<slug>
parameters.description: Range filter, `from..to`; either end may be omitted.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: relevance | newest | price_asc | price_desc | distance. An explicit sort never receives a promotional boost.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Registered doc_type. One type per query — federated search across types is not in v1.

post.summary: Re-pull specific keys, or rebuild a whole document type

get.description:
``GET /search/api/v1/suggest`` — what to offer under the search box.

``categories`` is the primary half: each row is a destination with its
full ancestor path and the number of listings a buyer would actually
see there, ranked by that number. ``terms`` is the title-prefix half.

Neither comes from a query log: no query log is kept, which is a privacy
decision before it is a product one, and on day one there would be
nothing in it anyway.

The answer is public, identical for every reader and requested on every
keystroke, so it carries ``Cache-Control: public`` and an ``ETag``. This
is the module's first conditional read — ``query`` has none, because a
SERP answer embeds ``took_ms`` and a cursor and would revalidate to a
miss every time. Here the payload is deliberately free of anything that
varies with the clock.

**Permissions:** `AllowAny`
get.summary: Type-ahead: category paths with live counts, plus title prefixes

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Language of the query: picks the dictionary, so «shorty» reaches «шорты». Falls back to Accept-Language, then DEFAULT_LANGUAGE.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per half. Capped by MAX_SUGGEST_LIMIT.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What the buyer has typed so far.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Registered doc_type. Optional when exactly one type is registered — a type-ahead should not have to name the only corpus there is.

CategorySuggestion.description: One destination in the dropdown, ready to render and ready to follow.

id.description: Category id. A `listings`-graded row derives it from the path's leaf segment.

slug.description: Category slug. Empty on a `listings`-graded row: no comm Function in the fleet resolves a path id to its slug or name yet.

name.description: The category's own display name. On a `listings`-graded row this is the leaf id as a truthful segment — render such rows by their `count` instead.

path.description: Display names root->leaf, e.g. ['Мужская одежда', 'Шорты']. This is what distinguishes three categories that share a name. `listings`-graded rows carry the id segments here.

category.description: The ancestry as ids joined with '/'. Pass it verbatim as the `category` parameter of /query — do not re-join path segments yourself.

count.description: Live listings a buyer would see under this category, descendants included — the same number the SERP reports for it. On a `listings`-graded row: how many of them match the typed query, which is the count a `?q=…&category=…` tap will show.

match.description:
How the row earned its place: the four name grades from `categories.suggest`, or `listings` — a goods-driven row, offered because documents matching the query live there even though no category name says the word. Ranking: strong grades (exact/prefix/word) and `listings` sort as one class above `substring`; within a class, stocked before empty, then grade, then count desc, then depth, then name.

* `exact` - exact
* `prefix` - prefix
* `word` - word
* `substring` - substring
* `listings` - listings

FacetLabels.description: Captions for one slug's option codes.

translatable.description: True when `values` holds translation KEYS to run through the catalogue; false when it holds literal captions. The reader cannot tell by looking — `b.apple` and `Б/у` are both strings.

approximate.description: True when counts came from a sample because the candidate set exceeded FACET_CANDIDATE_CAP.

candidates.description: Size of the largest counted set.

skipped.description: Plan slugs dropped at MAX_FACET_FIELDS — reported, not vanished.

dropped_filters.description: `f.<slug>`/`r.<slug>` filters this answer did NOT apply, because the category marks the slug non-public (`FeatureDef.visibility` is `owner` or `staff`). A hidden value is not indexed and is not filterable: letting `?f.vin=<value>` through would make the index an exact-match oracle over an identifier. The answer is wider than what was asked for, and says so here rather than silently.

core_ranges.description: Range slugs that address a core document column rather than an attribute (`r.price`). Offer them as filters unconditionally: they exist for every document in every category, which is why they are not in the category's own plan.

RankingResponse.description: The P2B Art. 5 disclosure, generated from the scorer registry.

keys.description: Re-pull exactly these keys; omit to rebuild the whole type.

active.description: False when the configured engine cannot evaluate this parameter.

score.description: Ranking score; 0 under an explicit sort.

promoted.description: Whether this result is promoted. Present on EVERY item under EVERY sort, including when false — a mandatory marking (DSA Art. 26), not an optional field.

distance_km.description: Great-circle distance from the searched centre.

card.description: Stored row fields, so a result page costs one query.

SearchResponse.description: The query envelope: AnchorPagination's keys, plus what search owes.

facets.description: {slug: {value: count}}, counted with the slug's own filter removed.

facet_labels.description: {slug: {translatable, values: {value: caption}}} for slugs whose options are inline in the category schema. Absent for a vocabulary-backed slug: its level lives outside the schema and the plan will not invent a caption it has not read.

count.description: How many documents match. NEVER 0 beside a non-empty items[] — the answer may not claim fewer matches than the page shows. `null` means the engine cannot say, and is rendered as no count at all.

count_is_lower_bound.description: True when `count` is a floor: at least this many match, possibly more (a capped count, a window-truncated engine answer). Render 'N+', never 'N'.

exact_total.description: True when `count` is exact for THIS answer — equivalent to `count is not null and not count_is_lower_bound`. Per answer, not per engine: an engine without a guaranteed exact total still counts a small candidate set exactly.

degraded.description: What the configured engine could not do for this query.

language.description: The language whose dictionary and analyzer configuration answered — `lang`, else Accept-Language, else DEFAULT_LANGUAGE. When the fallback is wrong the synonym layer silently does not apply, and this field is the only place the answer says so.

categories.description: Destinations, ranked by match class (strong name grades and goods-driven rows above substring), then stocked before empty, then grade, then live listing count desc, then depth, then name.

items.description: Deprecated alias of `terms`, kept for one minor.

language.description: Which dictionary answered — the same resolution /query reports.

degraded.description: What this answer could not do: `category_suggestions` (no provider for category names), `category_rollup` (no ancestry, so counts would read 0), `category_listing_suggestions` (no name matched and the configured engine does not implement the optional goods-driven verb, or it failed).
